Task Manager

A Java and PostgreSQL task manager over JDBC — full CRUD, prepared statements, and a schema designed from scratch.
Author

Khang Thai

Published

January 26, 2025

Java PostgreSQL JDBC SQL

A deliberately small project with a deliberate purpose: build the database layer by hand. No ORM, no framework — just Java, JDBC, and a PostgreSQL schema I designed myself, so that every query and every connection is something I had to reason about.

Schema design

  • Designed a PostgreSQL tasks table with columns for task ID, name, description, due date and status.
  • Chose types and constraints up front rather than letting a migration tool decide them.

JDBC integration

  • Established the JDBC connection and wrote the SQL for insert, select, update and delete directly.
  • Used prepared statements throughout — parameterized queries, so user input never reaches the database as concatenated SQL. This is the whole reason to write the layer by hand: SQL injection stops being an abstract lesson.

Application

  • Add a task with name, description, due date and status.
  • View every task currently persisted.
  • Update a task's name or status.
  • Delete a task permanently.
  • Wrapped in a console interface that prompts for each operation.

Where it goes next

The natural extensions are user authentication, filtering and sorting on the query side, and a real front end. The backend is already structured so that swapping the console for an HTTP layer would not require rewriting the data access code.
